note: THE DIVERGENCE `multibyte-string-p' COSTS, asked of `s-reverse' ITSELF rather than of the naive reversal beside it -- and it is written to STAY. The subject is `e' followed by COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT (U+0301), two characters that render as one grapheme. Emacs answers ("e\u0301" (101 769) (101 769)): `multibyte-string-p' is `t' there, so `s-reverse' takes the MULTIBYTE branch, `(require 'ucs-normalize)' and walks whole grapheme clusters, and the sequence comes back UNCHANGED. kg answers ("\u0301e" (769 101) (101 769)): `multibyte-string-p' answers nil by decision (frontier-multibyte-string-p-non-ascii), so `s-reverse' takes the else branch, `(concat (nreverse (string-to-list s)))', which is a CHARACTER reversal -- right for "h\u00e9llo" (frontier-s-el-reverse-route agrees) and wrong here, because it puts the accent before the letter it modifies. THE THIRD ELEMENT IS THE CONTROL: both sides read the input as the same two codepoints, so the divergence is the BRANCH and not the decoding. This case exists because the frontier demand phase's F.1a found the divergence recorded only in prose -- frontier-s-reverse-grapheme-cluster asks the naive reversal, which both sides now perform identically, and flipped. Closing this one needs a grapheme-cluster surface and `ucs-normalize', which no demand in this phase's six wants asks for; kg carries no Unicode tables at all.
